scope: 73 cleaned TRACE PIAs; exploratory content characterization only
discovery_topic_names: Unauthorized access or disclosure of personal information
Purpose-incompatible use and downstream misuse of personal information
Insufficient privacy notice, awareness, or meaningful consent
Limits on individual access, correction, deletion, and redress
Data quality, classification, integrity, and availability failures
refinement_decision: Retained eight failure-mechanism themes and explicit boundary rules, preventing broad discovery labels from obscuring access-versus-use, accuracy-versus-redress, and notice-versus-post-collection-rights distinctions.

topics.name: Excessive or intrusive collection and inference
topics.definition: The system collects, combines, derives, monitors, or concentrates more, more sensitive, or more identifiable information than a demonstrated purpose requires, including unnecessarily intrusive surveillance or profiling.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Too much is acquired or derived means R01; wrong later purpose means R03; too long means R05.

topics.name: Security compromise and unauthorized access
topics.definition: A person or process without the required identity, entitlement, or permission may reach, view, alter, extract, destroy, or disrupt information, or the system or data may be compromised through a security failure.
exclusion_rule: incompatible handling by an authorized user or recipient
disclosure or public-release boundary as the central mechanism
record error without a security event
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Who can reach the data means R02; what an otherwise participating user or recipient may do with it or where it is sent means R03.

topics.name: Incompatible use, disclosure, or external custody
topics.definition: Information may be used beyond its approved purpose, disclosed to an inappropriate recipient, made public, redistributed, or placed with another organization or platform in ways that weaken purpose and recipient boundaries.
inclusion_rule: disclosure without authority, consent, or need
exclusion_rule: notice or consent deficits without a handling boundary
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Use, recipient, purpose, or location boundary means R03; identity, entitlement, or access boundary means R02.

topics.name: Inaccurate, incomplete, stale, or unreliable information
topics.definition: Records, inputs, linkages, or analytical outputs may be incorrect, incomplete, obsolete, inconsistent, biased, or otherwise unreliable and may produce an inappropriate analysis, communication, or decision.
inclusion_rule: biased or unrepresentative inputs when stated
exclusion_rule: security compromise without a quality consequence
compliance consequence without a quality defect
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Defect in record or output means R04; inability to inspect, challenge, or correct it means R07.

topics.name: Excessive retention or failed disposition
topics.definition: Identifiable information may remain beyond operational or legal need, lack an enforceable lifecycle endpoint, or fail to be deleted, overwritten, returned, archived, or destroyed as required.
inclusion_rule: failure to dispose at end of purpose
exposure explicitly increased by extended retention
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Time, lifecycle endpoint, or disposition failure must be central; otherwise use the explicit harm category or R_UNCLEAR.

topics.name: Insufficient notice, understanding, or meaningful choice
topics.definition: Individuals may not know or understand collection, monitoring, sponsorship, use, sharing, or consequences, or may lack a meaningful opportunity to consent, decline, opt out, or authorize participation.
inclusion_rule: no meaningful consent, refusal, or opt-out
invalid representative authorization as a choice problem
exclusion_rule: post-collection access, amendment, challenge, or remedy
incompatible use or disclosure where notice is not the stated problem
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Understanding and choice before or at collection or use means R06; post-collection rights mean R07.

topics.name: Barriers to access, correction, challenge, or redress
topics.definition: After information is maintained or acted upon, an individual may be unable to inspect it, correct or amend or delete it where applicable, challenge a decision or disputed record, or obtain a usable remedy.
inclusion_rule: missing or cumbersome access and amendment procedures
inability to remove public or third-party content
exclusion_rule: inaccurate record without a rights barrier
lack of initial notice or consent
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Bad data means R04; inability to fix or challenge it means R07.

topics.name: Weak governance, accountability, or compliance capacity
topics.definition: Privacy protection may fail because duties, policies, ownership, workforce knowledge, documentation, oversight, or enforceability are absent or inadequate.
inclusion_rule: weak partner oversight without a concrete disclosure event
inability to demonstrate or enforce compliance
exclusion_rule: concrete access, use, disclosure, or rights failure merely accompanied by legal consequences
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Organizational capacity or duty failure means R08; an explicit concrete privacy event takes its mechanism code primary.

topics.name: Other substantive risk
topics.definition: Clear substantive privacy failure mechanism outside R01-R08; record a proposed theme.
topics.inclusion_rule: Clear substantive privacy failure mechanism outside R01-R08; record a proposed theme.
topics.exclusion_rule: Use a named substantive topic whenever supported.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Clear substantive privacy failure mechanism outside R01-R08; record a proposed theme.

topics.name: Unclear or ambiguous risk
topics.definition: Genuine risk language but no mechanism or no defensible dominant mechanism.
topics.inclusion_rule: Genuine risk language but no mechanism or no defensible dominant mechanism.
topics.exclusion_rule: Use a named substantive topic whenever supported.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Genuine risk language but no mechanism or no defensible dominant mechanism.

topics.name: Non-substantive risk text
topics.definition: Non-risk content, null or assurance-only statement, prompt, heading, bare category list, bare severity, cross-reference, or extraction artefact.
topics.inclusion_rule: Non-risk content, null or assurance-only statement, prompt, heading, bare category list, bare severity, cross-reference, or extraction artefact.
topics.exclusion_rule: Use a named substantive topic whenever supported.
topics.nearest_competitor: See tie-break and priority confusion pairs.
topics.distinction_rule: Non-risk content, null or assurance-only statement, prompt, heading, bare category list, bare severity, cross-reference, or extraction artefact.
